# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

## Outcomes

Source: partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (both PROPOSED, not accepted).
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with four scaffold packages: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (basis: SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (basis: index row count × request rate; not measured); measured on a sample by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured on a sample by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). One track: each outcome consumes the previous one's output.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index core
      Objective: Ingest one closed quarter's quarterly index and one week of daily indexes from the SEC into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (scaffold only)
      Produces: a filing-index table holding those real rows, readable by Stage 2; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds the quarter's and the week's rows, with row counts per source file; the findings file records the files fetched, bytes, request count and elapsed time of the real run.
      Leaves out: full history and daily catch-up → Stage 4; raw-byte retention, replay, reconciliation and versioned publication → Stage 5; a shared request budget across collectors → Stage 6; scheduling, deployment and monitoring → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions on a sample
      Objective: Download the submissions named by a sample of Stage 1's index rows.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the sample's submissions on disk, each traceable to its index row; measured per-file time and bytes
      Exit: O2 — every sampled row has a downloaded submission or a recorded failure reason; the measured per-file time and bytes replace O2's full-history cost estimate.
      Leaves out: full history, resume after interruption and a shared request budget → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K on the sample
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's downloaded submissions
      Produces: extracted main documents for the sample's 10-K and 8-K filings; measured extraction time
      Exit: O3 — each 10-K and 8-K in the sample has an extracted main document or a recorded failure reason; the measured extraction time per filing is recorded.
      Leaves out: extraction over all downloaded submissions → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index full history and daily continuation
      Objective: Extend the filing-index table to the chosen backfill range and catch daily indexes up after missed days.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's table and findings
      Produces: a filing-index table covering the chosen range, with a per-source report of gaps
      Exit: O1 — the table covers the chosen range and the report lists every unresolved gap; a run after a skipped window ingests the missed days without losing older work.
      Leaves out: replay, reconciliation and versioned publication → Stage 5; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Index replay, reconciliation and publication
      Objective: Make the index table replayable from stored bytes, reconciled against later quarterly changes, and published as complete versions.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's full-range table
      Produces: stored original index bytes; a published, versioned filing index that readers resolve without scanning files
      Exit: O1 — a reparse from stored bytes makes no SEC requests and yields the same rows; a changed quarterly file is recorded as additions, updates or gated withdrawals; readers see only complete versions.
      Leaves out: scheduling and alerting → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Submissions at scale
      Objective: Download the submissions for the chosen range, resumably, with every SEC request sharing one budget.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2's findings; Stage 4's full-range table
      Produces: the chosen range's submissions on disk, with a per-submission status
      Exit: O2 — an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed submissions; the measured request rate across all collectors stays at or below the configured target; measured throughput and total bytes are recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduling and alerting → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: 10-K and 8-K at scale
      Objective: Extract the main documents of every 10-K and 8-K among the downloaded submissions.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 3's findings; Stage 6's submissions
      Produces: extracted main documents for all downloaded 10-K and 8-K filings, with a per-filing status
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in the downloaded set has an extracted main document or a recorded failure reason; the total extraction time is recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduling and alerting → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduled operation
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, reconciliation and new-submission handling on a schedule, with monitoring, on a platform still to be chosen (the background ADR is proposed, not accepted).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 5, 6 and 7
      Produces: scheduled runs with durable reports and failure alerts
      Exit: O1, O2, O3 — observed scheduled runs, not manual ones, produce reports that show new index rows, downloaded submissions and extracted 10-K/8-K documents; a forced failure raises an alert.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

With every stage ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list: a verdict per outcome with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Each unmet outcome becomes a new stage or a written deferral before this roadmap retires.
